text:
Sara K.: Hey team — customer (Acme Analytics) says their Azure Accelerator credits show in the Azure portal but their Redwood balance is 0. They activated the accelerator on 2026-03-10 and sent the marketplace order id `AZ-ORD-99871`. Screenshot attached in ticket.
Matt B.: @Sara can you share the account id and subscription id? I want to check our entitlement ledger first.
Sara K.: Account: acct-0a1b2c3d, subscription: sub-77a4. Customer says the subscription was created under a different tenant alias than their billing tenant.
Raj P.: Thanks. Quick repro attempt — I tried to call our internal credit-apply endpoint with the marketplace order id and got a 400: `{"error":"entitlement_not_found","order_id":"AZ-ORD-99871"}`. Repro steps:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/internal/credits/apply \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat /secrets/admin_token)" \
  -d '{"marketplace_order_id":"AZ-ORD-99871","account_id":"acct-0a1b2c3d"}'
```
Response: `400 entitlement_not_found`
Matt B.: Hmm — checking finance ledger for subscription `sub-77a4`... ledger shows no marketplace redemption row for that order id. Partner side claim says redeemed on 2026-03-10.
AzureBot: Webhook delivery failed for incoming entitlement webhook from azure-marketplace. Error: `403 Signature verification failed` — payload: `{"order_id":"AZ-ORD-99871","subscription_id":"sub-77a4"}`. Retry attempted 3/3.
Cleo (partner): Hi all — I see the order on the Azure publisher portal marked as Completed on 2026-03-10 for subscription `sub-77a4`. Publisher order id `PUB-4422`. We pushed the entitlement but our system got a 403 from Redwood's webhook endpoint. Can you confirm your webhook signing key? We rotated keys last month.
Raj P.: That explains it — our webhook handler rejects signatures that use the older `x-azure-signature-v2` header format. The customer used the older header due to a partner-side SDK. I can patch the handler to accept both `v1` and `v2` signatures and add a tolerant check for tenant alias mapping. Proposed change:
- accept `x-azure-signature-v1` OR `x-azure-signature-v2`
- if signature fails, log full raw payload and email ops instead of dropping silently
- fallback mapping for tenant alias -> canonical tenant id
Matt B.: Sounds good. @finance FYI: don't mark as applied until webhook verification is green. I've opened ticket SUP-58291 and flagged as P2 (escalation). Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-58291
Sara K.: Customer is getting anxious. Can we do a manual apply while fix is rolled? If we map `AZ-ORD-99871` -> acct-0a1b2c3d and apply 30k credits, they should be unblocked.
Raj P.: I'll do a manual apply now and add an audit note. Running internal tool:
```
# apply credits (internal admin tool)
apply_credits --account acct-0a1b2c3d --order AZ-ORD-99871 --amount 30000 --reason "manual apply: webhook failure"
```
Result: `OK — credits applied, ledger row id L-20260312-7001`
Cleo (partner): Great — I can confirm we see a successful callback now that Raj retried with the patched signature handler in staging. We'll coordinate key rotation next week.
Matt B.: Finance verified ledger row L-20260312-7001 and updated billing balance. @Sara please confirm with customer.
Sara K.: Customer confirmed: balance reflected and API calls now succeed. They appreciated the manual apply. Marking resolved pending rollout of the signature-tolerant fix to prod. Closing ticket SUP-58291 after prod deploy.
Raj P.: Follow-ups: (1) PR #4437 to accept v2 signatures + tenant alias mapping; (2) postmortem note in #incidents explaining webhook observability gap; (3) add a temporary dashboard alert for webhook 4xx spikes.
Sara K.: Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
